extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and applicants prosecuting patents in Brazil (including foreign counsel used to the US system)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on Brazil-specific rules and practice for prosecuting patent applications before the INPI, including expedited-examination programmes, amendment rules, divisional timing and scope, and using court actions to accelerate prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: INPI expedited examination programmes (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: The INPI has multiple examination acceleration programmes (PPH with USPTO and JPO, green patents, health products, small companies, potential infringement, elderly applicant) intended to reduce backlog and speed up examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programmes aim to shorten examination times (approximately 18 months after a request to participate). Some are pilot initiatives with technical-area restrictions; others (eg green patents) are not pilots and have fewer restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) programme requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PPH programmes are pilot initiatives and apply to specific technical areas and additional requirements (classification under a specific IPC section; US/Japanese counterpart applications require notices of allowance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The INPI-JPO PPH applies only to information technology; the INPI-USPTO PPH applies only to oil and gas. Applicants must meet the technical-area and IPC-classification requirements and provide counterpart notices of allowance where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green patents programme requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Green applications must refer to an environmentally friendly technology and include no more than 15 claims, three of which may be independent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The green patents programme is not a pilot and does not require notices of allowance for counterpart applications; applicants may file a request to participate immediately after requesting examination in Brazil, making it relatively easy to access and typically effective (~18 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other INPI acceleration programmes (health products, small companies, potential infringement, elderly applicant)
rubrics_metrics.description: INPI runs targeted programmes for applications relating to public health products/processes/equipment/materials, for small Brazilian companies, where a third party is using the invention (potential infringement), and for applicants aged 60 or above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programmes are separate tracks to speed examination. Eligibility depends on subject matter or applicant status; specific operational details may vary and should be checked before filing a request to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using court action to expedite examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants can file federal court actions to compel the INPI to decide within a reasonable timeframe; courts commonly grant orders requiring the INPI to issue a decision (often within 60 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court proceedings typically assess whether an administrative decision is overdue; hearings are usually short and a judicial decision is normally obtained within two to four months. Court orders are used solely to compel expedited examination and generally do not jeopardise the applicant's relationship with the INPI or lead to unfavourable substantive outcomes; existing case law favours such measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination request deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: An examination request must be filed within 36 months from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deadline is critical because certain amendment and divisional-filing rights differ before vs after the examination request is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary modifications before filing an examination request
rubrics_metrics.description: Before filing an examination request, applicants may modify the patent application, including adding or cancelling claims, adjusting claim categories, adding or removing features, and re-writing entire portions of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pre-examination period to adjust scope and claim structure broadly; many substantive changes are permitted during this phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary modifications after filing an examination request (restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once examination is requested, it is impossible to increase the claim's scope and several restrictions apply: applicants are prohibited from removing features from the claims, changing the category of a claim, or adding new independent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite prohibitions on broadening, applicants may include dependent claims, include features in independent or dependent claims that are supported by the specification or other claims (drawings do not provide support), and remove features/words/phrases for the purpose of overcoming lack of clarity. Plan substantive claim-scope changes before the examination request is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support requirements for claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Features added after examination request must be supported by the specification and other claims; drawings do not provide support for claim amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting and amending claims, ensure added matter finds explicit support in the written description or existing claims; reliance on drawings for support is not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications — timing under law and INPI practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Brazilian law, a patent application may be divided up until the end of the examination procedures, but the INPI has ruled divisions are allowed only until a notice of allowance or a pre-appeal rejection is issued; once an appeal is filed against a rejection, the applicant may not divide the application per the INPI rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many practitioners consider the INPI rule contrary to federal law and potentially illegal; however, without successful legal challenge applicants should file divisional applications before the appeal phase or before a notice of allowance is issued to preserve divisional rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications — scope and permitted content
rubrics_metrics.description: Before requesting examination, applicants may file a divisional and amend claims in both original and divisional applications. Once examination is requested, applicants can only 'slice' the original to create a divisional: they must choose one or more existing claims from the parent to form the divisional and are prohibited from including new claims in the divisional or modifying existing claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the divisional application is filed, voluntary modifications to the divisional's claims are permitted. Plan the parent application's claim set carefully prior to requesting examination if divisional flexibility is required.
